issues.description: The template and problem statement expect getAllPersons to return a List<Person> (and sorting is described as producing an ordered result), but the solution changes the service signature to return Set<Person>. Meanwhile PersonResource in the solution still declares ResponseEntity<List<Person>> as its return type and forwards the Set result from the service. This creates a compile-time type mismatch and also loses ordering semantics (converting the sorted list to a HashSet destroys the sort order). This contradicts the problem requirement that sorting of persons be supported and returned to the client as an ordered collection.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the return type consistent and preserve ordering: change PersonService.getAllPersons to return a List<Person> (or Collection preserving order) and avoid converting the sorted list into a HashSet. Then return that List from PersonResource (ResponseEntity<List<Person>>). Alternatively, if a Set is intentionally desired, update PersonResource's signature to ResponseEntity<Set<Person>> and ensure the service returns a Set implementation that preserves iteration order (e.g. LinkedHashSet) — but preserving an ordered List is the clearer fix to satisfy the sorting requirement.
